chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Jarrah al-Hazza', from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, who said:

Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever performs wudu for the Maghrib prayer, that wudu of his is an expiation for what has passed of his sins during his day, except the major sins; and whoever performs wudu for the Fajr (morning) prayer, that wudu of his is an expiation for what has passed of his sins during his night, except the major sins.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of performing wudu before Maghrib and Fajr prayers?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam Musa al-Kazim (peace be upon him) elucidates the spiritual efficacy of wudu as a means of expiation (kaffarah) for minor sins, distinguishing between the day's transgressions at Maghrib and the night's at Fajr. This teaching underscores the Shia emphasis on the purifying power of ritual purity, provided major sins (al-kaba'ir) are excluded, linking physical cleanliness with spiritual renewal in daily devotional practice.
